description: Fist-sized lump of glossy black glass, cooled out of some fire-thing's crust. Keen enough to shave with, so don't.
lore: Knapped into flakes it gives the finest edge in the trade and survives about four minutes of work. Steel drags; glass parts. When you are opening a broken shape for what sits at the bottom of it, drag is what scars a stone, and a scarred stone loses a third of its price — so the careful carry a lump and strike a fresh flake off it as they go, using each until it dulls and dropping it where they kneel.

Which means a working site glitters. Come up a hillside at low sun and you can read exactly where somebody stopped, how long they took over it, and from the count of flakes how much trouble the shape gave them. [[lore/the_hard_pieces|Cracking]] is a private profession that leaves the tidiest record of itself of any work in Nangijala, and the trade has never managed to break the habit.
